APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 1 - Panel Workshop Safety and Body Construction                               v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_1_Task_3_Panel_Workshop_Safety_and_Body_Construction_v1.0
 Block                    Block 1 - Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills - Shared Controlled Programme
 Weeks                Weeks 1-10 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1, D2, D5, D8, D9, D10
 KSBs covered           K2, K3, K6, K8, K9, S1, S6, S7, B1-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A damaged vehicle or training shell has arrived for an initial panel-shop inspection. You must prepare the work area, select
suitable PPE, identify vehicle body construction features and record safety-related findings before any repair work begins.

 Objectives

 - Prepare the workstation using safe bodyshop routines and PPE.
 - Identify body construction, panel type and visible safety-system concerns.
 - Apply COSHH, manual handling and housekeeping controls before work.
 - Record findings clearly using job-card and evidence expectations.
 - Explain when work must stop and be escalated to a supervisor.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Training vehicle, body shell or panel section
 - PPE, risk assessment template and COSHH information
 - Body construction diagrams or technical data
 - Inspection lamp, trim tools, measuring tape or gap gauge
 - Apprentice Assessment Record





v1.0

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 1 - Tool Control, Damage Documentation and Evidence Capture               v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_1_Task_4_Tool_Control_Damage_Documentation_and_Evidence_Capture_v1.0
 Block                    Block 1 - Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills - Shared Controlled Programme
 Weeks                Weeks 1-10 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1, D2, D5, D8, D9, D10
 KSBs covered           K2, K3, K6, K8, K9, S1, S6, S7, B1-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A vehicle has minor outer-panel damage. You must prepare tools, record damage accurately, capture evidence and
complete the documentation needed for a repair plan without carrying out structural repair.

 Objectives

 - Select and check panel repair tools before use.
 - Record visible damage using accurate bodyshop terminology.
 - Capture photo and document evidence suitable for portfolio upload.
 - Control fasteners, clips and small parts during inspection.
 - Demonstrate professional housekeeping and tool control.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Training vehicle or damaged panel
 - Panel repair hand tools and tool-control checklist
 - Camera or tablet for photo evidence
 - Job card, repair record and evidence log
 - PPE and safe storage equipment

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 2 - Damage Assessment and Repair Planning                                     v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_2_Task_3_Damage_Assessment_and_Repair_Planning_v1.0
 Block                    Block 2 - Panel Identification, Damage Assessment and Repair Planning
 Weeks                Weeks 11-28 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1-D5, D8, D10
 KSBs covered           K1-K5, K8, S1-S3, S5-S7, B1, B2, B5-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A customer vehicle has visible accident damage to an outer panel. You must assess the damage, use technical
information, decide whether repair or replacement is appropriate and prepare a repair-plan recommendation.

 Objectives

 - Assess visible panel damage using a structured routine.
 - Use technical data to inform repair-versus-replace decisions.
 - Identify safety systems, materials and possible supplementary damage.
 - Record labour, parts and authorisation requirements.
 - Communicate repair recommendations clearly and professionally.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Damaged vehicle, panel or training rig
 - OEM repair methods or technical data access
 - Damage assessment sheet and job card
 - Inspection lamp, straight edge and measuring equipment
 - PPE and camera/tablet for evidence

 Duties covered          D1-D5, D8, D10
 KSBs covered           K1-K5, K8, S1-S3, S5-S7, B1, B2, B5-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A bolt-on panel is scheduled for removal or replacement. You must prepare the vehicle safely, control fixings, check
adjacent panels and identify any supplementary damage before refit or handover.

 Objectives

 - Prepare a vehicle safely for bolt-on panel work.
 - Remove or prepare a bolt-on panel using an organised process.
 - Identify hidden or supplementary damage during disassembly.
 - Record fastener, clip, corrosion and sealing requirements.
 - Prepare clear handover information for MET, paint or supervisor review.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Training vehicle with bolt-on panel
 - Trim tools, hand tools, fixings tray and labels
 - Gap gauge, straight edge and inspection lamp
 - Job card, supplementary damage form and camera/tablet
 - PPE and protection materials

  Practical task instructions

1. Confirm the panel to be removed or prepared and protect adjacent areas.
2. Remove fixings methodically, storing clips and fasteners in a labelled system.
3. Inspect hidden areas, mounting points, corrosion protection and adjacent panel condition.
4. Record supplementary damage and identify any effect on the repair plan.
5. Complete the handover record and reinstate or secure the vehicle safely.

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 3 - Door or Wing Remove/Refit and Alignment                                     v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_3_Task_3_Door_or_Wing_Remove_Refit_and_Alignment_v1.0
 Block                    Block 3 - Non-Structural Panel Removal, Refit and Alignment
 Weeks                Weeks 29-42 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1, D4, D5, D8, D9
 KSBs covered           K3, K4, K6, K8, K9, S1, S5-S7, B1, B2, B4, B6, B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A non-structural bolt-on panel requires remove/refit and alignment. You must follow a safe method, control fasteners, set
panel gaps and confirm the final fit against adjacent panels.

 Objectives

 - Remove and refit a bolt-on panel using safe workshop practice.
 - Measure and record initial and final gap/flushness readings.
 - Use correct fixings, torque discipline and adjustment methods.
 - Identify causes of poor alignment or fit.
 - Complete a quality check before vehicle release or paint handover.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Training vehicle with door, wing, bonnet or tailgate
 - Hand tools, trim tools, torque wrench and fixings tray
 - Gap gauges, straight edge and alignment reference data
 - Panel protection materials and PPE
 - Remove/refit checklist and assessment record

 Task Reference          Block_3_Task_4_Bumper_Cover_Seals_and_Quality_Gate_Inspection_v1.0
 Block                    Block 3 - Non-Structural Panel Removal, Refit and Alignment

 Scenario

A bumper cover or trim assembly has been removed and refitted as part of a panel repair. You must check fixings, sensor
connections, seals, gap/flushness and final quality before the job moves to the next stage.

 Objectives

 - Inspect a refitted bumper cover or trim assembly for secure fitment.
 - Check clips, brackets, seals and connectors for damage or poor routing.
 - Confirm panel gaps, flushness and water/wind-noise risk points.
 - Record defects and rectification actions clearly.
 - Prepare the vehicle for paint, MET or customer handover.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Training vehicle with bumper/trim assembly
 - Trim tools, clip kit, inspection lamp and mirror
 - Gap gauge, straight edge and water-test equipment if available
 - Job card, quality checklist and camera/tablet
 - PPE and protection materials

 Task Reference           Block_4_Task_3_Technical_Data_Material_Identification_and_Repair_Method_Selection_v1.0
 Block                    Block 4 - Materials, Technical Data and Repair-Method Selection
 Weeks                Weeks 43-56 (source plan)

 Scenario

A damaged panel requires a method-based repair decision. You must identify the material, locate the correct repair
information, record restrictions and select a repair method that follows technical data.

 Objectives

 - Locate and interpret relevant technical data for panel repair.
 - Identify panel material and repair restrictions.
 - Select an appropriate repair route based on the method.
 - Record heat, joining and corrosion-protection requirements.
 - Explain why method discipline is critical on modern vehicles.

 - OEM repair methods or approved technical information
 - Material samples, panel sections or vehicle body diagram
 - Repair-method worksheet and job card
 - Inspection lamp, magnet where appropriate and PPE
 - Camera/tablet for evidence capture

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 4 - Joining Process Selection and Method Deviation Record                    v1.0




 Task Reference           Block_4_Task_4_Joining_Process_Selection_and_Method_Deviation_Record_v1.0
 Block                    Block 4 - Materials, Technical Data and Repair-Method Selection
 Weeks                Weeks 43-56 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1-D3, D5, D6, D8
 KSBs covered           K2, K3, K5, K7, K8, S1-S4, S6-S7, B1, B5-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A panel joint requires a decision on welding, bonding, riveting or another joining process. You must use the repair method,
check access and material requirements, then record any proposed deviation for approval.

 Objectives

 - Compare joining processes against method and material requirements.
 - Select tooling, settings and controls suitable for the joint.
 - Identify when a method deviation needs authorisation.
 - Complete a clear method deviation or approval record.
 - Explain quality and safety risks linked to incorrect joining.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - OEM repair method and joining process guidance
 - Joining equipment, access diagrams or training joint
 - Deviation/approval form and job card
 - PPE, extraction and fire-control equipment
 - Test-piece or QA checklist

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 5 - Spot Weld Removal and Weld Test Piece Quality Check                    v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_5_Task_3_Spot_Weld_Removal_and_Weld_Test_Piece_Quality_Check_v1.0
 Block                    Block 5 - Welding, Brazing, Bonding and Riveting
 Weeks                Weeks 57-71 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1, D3, D5, D6, D8, D9
 KSBs covered           K3, K5, K6, K7, K8, K9, S1, S3, S4, S6, S7, B1, B2, B6, B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

You are preparing a training joint for panel replacement. You must remove spot welds without damaging the flange,
prepare the joint and complete a weld test piece with quality evidence.

 Objectives

 - Set up the work area safely for welding-related activity.
 - Remove spot welds while protecting the parent panel and flange.
 - Prepare a joint or test piece using the correct method.
 - Record welding settings, test results and defects.
 - Apply extraction, fire watch and PPE discipline throughout.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Welding bay or training bench
 - Spot weld drill, grinder and flange preparation tools
 - MIG/MAG or resistance spot welding equipment as appropriate
 - Weld test pieces, PPE, extraction and fire equipment
 - Weld record, QA checklist and camera/tablet

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS

 Task Reference           Block_5_Task_4_Bonding_Riveting_and_Hybrid_Joining_Test_Piece_v1.0
 Block                    Block 5 - Welding, Brazing, Bonding and Riveting
 Weeks                Weeks 57-71 (source plan)

 Scenario

A repair method specifies bonded and riveted joining. You must prepare a test piece, control surface preparation, apply
adhesive, fit rivets and complete a quality record before the process is used on a vehicle.

 Objectives

 - Prepare surfaces for adhesive bonding using a controlled method.
 - Select and fit suitable rivets or mechanical fixings.
 - Control adhesive open time, bead size and curing requirements.
 - Record product details and process evidence.
 - Inspect the completed joint against method and quality requirements.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Bonding and riveting kit
 - Panel test pieces or training joint
 - Approved adhesive, applicator tips and cleaning products
 - PPE, extraction/ventilation and waste controls
 - Product data sheet, method sheet and QA record

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 6 - Panel Pulling and Metal Finishing                                                v1.0




 Task Reference           Block_6_Task_3_Panel_Pulling_and_Metal_Finishing_v1.0
 Block                    Block 6 - Panel Repair, Pulling, Metal Finishing and Filler
 Weeks                Weeks 72-85 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1, D4-D6, D8, D9
 KSBs covered           K3, K4, K6, K8, K9, S1, S5-S7, B1, B2, B6, B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A damaged panel requires controlled dent reduction before finishing. You must inspect the damage, plan a pulling
approach, reduce the dent and record the contour and quality checks completed.

 Objectives

 - Assess panel damage and plan a safe pulling or repair approach.
 - Use suitable pulling and metal-finishing tools under supervision.
 - Reduce damage while protecting panel shape and material integrity.
 - Check contour, high/low spots and repair quality.
 - Record remaining defects and next repair-stage requirements.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Damaged panel, training panel or repair vehicle
 - Pulling equipment, hammer/dolly set and contour tools
 - Straight edge, guide coat or profile gauge
 - PPE, extraction and workshop protection equipment
 - Panel repair checklist and evidence log

 Task Reference           Block_6_Task_4_Filler_Application_Shaping_and_Paint_Handover_v1.0
 Block                    Block 6 - Panel Repair, Pulling, Metal Finishing and Filler
 Weeks                Weeks 72-85 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1, D4-D6, D8, D9
 KSBs covered           K3, K4, K6, K8, K9, S1, S5-S7, B1, B2, B6, B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A repaired panel requires filler finishing before paint preparation. You must prepare the substrate, mix and apply filler,
shape the repair, check for defects and complete a paint handover record.

 Objectives

 - Prepare the substrate before filler application.
 - Mix and apply filler using appropriate safety controls.
 - Shape and sand the repair using a controlled process.
 - Identify pinholes, feather-edge issues and contour defects.
 - Complete a clear paint handover and quality record.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Prepared panel or training panel
 - Filler, mixing board, applicators and sanding blocks
 - Abrasives, guide coat and contour checking tools
 - PPE, dust extraction and masking/protection materials
 - Paint handover checklist and camera/tablet

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 7 - Underbody Measurement and Misalignment Report                          v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_7_Task_3_Underbody_Measurement_and_Misalignment_Report_v1.0
 Block                    Block 7 - Structural Measurement, Jig Systems and Realignment
 Weeks                Weeks 86-100 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1-D3, D5, D7, D8, D9
 KSBs covered           K1, K2, K3, K5, K6, K8, K9, S1, S3, S6-S8, B1, B2, B6, B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A vehicle has suspected structural misalignment after impact. You must use datum information, take underbody or chassis
measurements and complete a misalignment report for supervisor review.

 Objectives

 - Prepare the vehicle and measuring area safely.
 - Use technical data to identify datum points and target measurements.
 - Take and record measurements using an approved process.
 - Identify deviations and possible impact paths.
 - Complete a clear misalignment report and escalation recommendation.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Vehicle, body shell or structural measuring rig
 - Measuring system, tram gauge or jig data
 - Technical data and datum sheets
 - PPE, lifting/support equipment and safety checklist
 - Misalignment report and camera/tablet

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 7 - Jig Setup, Controlled Pull Plan and Post-Check                               v1.0




 Task Reference           Block_7_Task_4_Jig_Setup_Controlled_Pull_Plan_and_Post_Check_v1.0
 Block                    Block 7 - Structural Measurement, Jig Systems and Realignment
 Weeks                Weeks 86-100 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1-D3, D5, D7, D8, D9
 KSBs covered           K1, K2, K3, K5, K6, K8, K9, S1, S3, S6-S8, B1, B2, B6, B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A vehicle or training structure is being set up for controlled realignment. You must identify mounting points, prepare a jig or
bench setup, plan a pull and record post-check measurements.

 Objectives

 - Set up measuring or jig equipment using safe working practice.
 - Identify mounting, clamping and anchoring requirements.
 - Prepare a controlled pull plan from measurement evidence.
 - Record post-pull or post-setup checks accurately.
 - Explain quality and safety limits during structural realignment.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Jig, bench system or training alignment rig
 - Clamps, brackets, pulling equipment and safety chains
 - Manufacturer data, set-up sheet and measuring record
 - PPE, exclusion zone controls and inspection equipment
 - Controlled pull plan and QA checklist

final-20261113-qa2--panel--b08-t3.pdf.instructions:
APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 8 - Advanced Material Controls and Aluminium Contamination Prevention        v1.0




 Task Reference           Block_8_Task_3_Advanced_Material_Controls_and_Aluminium_Contamination_Prevention_v1.0
 Block                    Block 8 - Advanced Materials, Safety Systems and Emerging Technology
 Weeks                Weeks 101-114 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1-D3, D5, D6, D8, D10
 KSBs covered           K2, K3, K5, K7, K8, S1-S4, S6-S7, B1, B5-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A modern vehicle contains aluminium, high-strength steel or mixed-material panels. You must identify the material, apply
safe contamination controls and decide whether the repair is within your competence or must be referred.

 Objectives

 - Identify advanced material types and repair boundaries.
 - Apply contamination controls for aluminium or mixed-material work.
 - Select dedicated tools and cleaning methods where required.
 - Record manufacturer warnings and escalation decisions.
 - Explain sustainability, waste and safety responsibilities.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Material samples, vehicle panel or technical diagram
 - Dedicated aluminium tool set or contamination-control example
 - OEM method information and material chart
 - Cleaning materials, PPE and waste controls
 - Material identification and referral record

APPRENTICE INSTRUCTIONS
Panel L3 Block 8 - ADAS, SRS and Alternative Fuel Safety Referral                              v1.0




 Task Reference          Block_8_Task_4_ADAS_SRS_and_Alternative_Fuel_Safety_Referral_v1.0
 Block                    Block 8 - Advanced Materials, Safety Systems and Emerging Technology
 Weeks                Weeks 101-114 (source plan)
 Duties covered          D1-D3, D5, D6, D8, D10
 KSBs covered           K2, K3, K5, K7, K8, S1-S4, S6-S7, B1, B5-B7
 Estimated duration      60 minutes
 Assessment type          Practical / knowledge / documentation

 Scenario

A damaged vehicle has visible safety-system, sensor or alternative fuel features near the repair area. You must identify
risks, record referral requirements and explain how these systems affect panel repair planning.

 Objectives

 - Identify visible ADAS, SRS and alternative fuel warning indicators.
 - Apply safe boundaries and referral decisions for high-risk systems.
 - Record calibration, isolation or specialist requirements.
 - Communicate limitations to a supervisor or repair planner.
 - Prepare a safe customer or workshop advisory note.
  Materials you need at the workstation

 - Vehicle, diagrams or training rig with safety-system features
 - Technical data, warning label examples and referral checklist
 - PPE and safe approach guidance
 - Job card, advisory note and camera/tablet
 - Supervisor review or sign-off record

action plan that links remaining gaps to the panel technician standard and EPA methods.
